item.description:
locations
US, CA, Santa Clara
time type
Full time
posted on
Posted Today
job requisition id
JR2024900
Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.
NVIDIA is seeking an extraordinary innovator in networking and system architecture to join our Research team. In this role, you will focus on designing networks optimized for AI systems, as well as leveraging AI and machine learning to advance network architecture and enable intelligent, real-time decision-making for tasks such as control, routing, congestion management, and scheduling.
We are seeking a balanced background of research excellence in building systems and a deep understanding and broad perspective across the fields of computer architecture and communication systems for distributed computation. NVIDIA is a technology leader in systems for Artificial Intelligence, and this research team invents new networking technologies to advance the performance, scalability, and efficiency of next-generation computing platforms. This position offers you the opportunity to have a real impact while working with some of the most creative and forward-thinking people in the world who are here at this dynamic, technology-focused company.
What you'll be doing:
Develop innovative network architectures, algorithms, and hardware/software co-design approaches for high-performance interconnects and large-scale distributed AI systems, including AI-assisted methods where appropriate, to enable efficient, scalable, and robust communication and extend the state of the art in networking, distributed computing, and system architecture.
Create and evaluate mechanisms for network and system decision-making in large-scale GPU/accelerator clusters, including AI/ML-based approaches for routing, traffic engineering, congestion control, scheduling, topology design, and telemetry-driven control loops.
Invent new techniques, technologies, methodologies, processes, and devices, to enable new products or types of products. Deliverable results include prototypes, patents, publications, and product impact.
Prototype new ideas in simulation or through analytical modeling.
Produce technology vision and the basis for products 5-10 years out. Focus should not be on products currently shipping or in development, except as to how they can be extended and improved.
Participate in the broader research community. Examples are serving as a reviewer or on Program Committees, publishing papers and speaking at conferences.
Collaborate with external researchers, primarily in academia, to encourage mutually beneficial work.
What we need to see:
Pursuing or recently completed a PhD in relevant discipline(s) (CS, CE, EE, Physics, Math) or equivalent experience.
2+ years of relevant industrial and academic experience preferred. Relevant experience includes systems and network design for AI or HPC infrastructure and/or applying AI/ML to systems or networking problems (e.g., optimization, reinforcement learning, graph learning, telemetry-driven control).
Background and publication record in systems, networking, computer architecture, and/or ML for networking/systems. Publication at venues such as ISCA, HPCA, MICRO, SIGCOMM, NSDI (and related venues) is a plus.
Signals of fit: evidence via publications plus artifacts (open-source, prototypes, production deployments) demonstrating impactful contributions to systems or network design for AI infrastructure, including where ML/RL informs design or drives online decisions.
Experience with AI/ML methods for systems and networks supporting AI workloads (e.g., PyTorch/TensorFlow/JAX) is valuable. It includes applying these methods to system or network building, simulation, optimization, and control/decision loops.
Strong programming and prototyping ability, with experience building research artifacts, simulators, or system prototypes; C++ and Python preferred, and experience with hardware description languages or HLS is desirable.
NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 168,000 USD - 264,500 USD.
You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.
Applications for this job will be accepted at least until September 22, 2026.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes.
NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

Job Details:
Job Description:
Why Intel Foundry
At Intel Foundry, you will help develop and enable next-generation silicon photonics technologies that power AI, cloud computing, networking, and high-speed communications. As part of a world-class engineering organization, you will work alongside leading scientists and engineers to solve complex reliability challenges, influence technology decisions, and bring innovative photonic technologies from research and development into high-volume manufacturing.
This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the industry's most advanced Silicon Photonics programs and help deliver reliable, cutting-edge solutions to Intel Foundry customers worldwide.
About the Role
Intel's Silicon Photonics Quality & Reliability team is seeking a Senior Silicon Photonics Reliability Engineer to drive reliability strategy, qualification, and technology development for advanced photonic devices and Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs).
In this role, you will partner closely with technology development, process integration, design, manufacturing, and quality teams to assess, improve, and certify the reliability of silicon photonics technologies and products. You will play a key role in identifying reliability risks, developing qualification methodologies, resolving complex technical challenges, and ensuring successful transitions from technology development to high-volume manufacturing.
What You’ll Do
Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:
Assess and characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic reliability of photonic devices, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), lasers, and integrated optical products.
Develop reliability models and acceleration methodologies through Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, and reliability testing.
Drive reliability improvements through process, design, and material optimization efforts.
Develop and implement new reliability characterization techniques, screening methodologies, and quality controls.
Define reliability, qualification, and certification requirements for new silicon photonics technologies and products.
Lead failure analysis and root cause investigations using data-driven and model-based problem-solving techniques.
Evaluate reliability risks and provide recommendations to engineering and business stakeholders.
Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure quality and reliability requirements are integrated throughout the technology development lifecycle.
Support new technology introduction and successful transfer into high-volume manufacturing environments.
Analyze large data sets to identify trends, opportunities, and reliability risks using advanced statistical methods.
Present technical findings and recommendations to engineering leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, and executive management.
Contribute to reliability strategy, best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives across Intel Foundry's Silicon Photonics organization.
The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:
Strong technical judgment and the ability to make sound decisions with incomplete information while appropriately balancing risk and business impact.
Ownership and accountability for driving complex technical initiatives from concept through implementation.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills with a structured, data-driven approach.
Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across engineering, manufacturing, quality, and business organizations.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for diverse audiences.
Capability to manage multiple priorities and execute effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Intellectual curiosity and a passion for developing innovative technologies.
Adaptability and resilience when navigating ambiguity and evolving business priorities.
A collaborative mindset and commitment to fostering an inclusive team environment.
Passion for quality, reliability, operational excellence, and customer success.
Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.
See Intel Benefits for more details.
Qualifications:
You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.
Note:
For information on Intel’s immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see
Intel U.S. Immigration Sponsorship Information
Minimum Qualifications and Experience:
Master's degree in Photonics/Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Semiconductor Engineering, or a related Stem degree with 4+ years of relevant experience. Or a PhD in in the same filed with 2+ years of relevant industry.
In addition, candidates should possess experience in one or more of the following areas:
2+ years of silicon photonics, photonic devices, optical devices, or integrated photonics technology development.
4+ years of semiconductor device characterization, validation, yield, reliability, or test engineering.
4+ years with compound semiconductor processing and photonic device physics.
4+ years of reliability engineering, qualification engineering, failure analysis, or technology development within semiconductor or photonics environments.
Preferred Qualifications and Experience:
PhD in Physics, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, or related engineering fields with 2+ years of experience in photonic devices.
Previous related work experience in a semiconductor foundry preferred.
Process certification/product qualification and reliability risk assessment, quality systems, and quality culture knowledge.
Semiconductor device physics and defect mechanism knowledge.
Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes, manufacturing process development, material characterization and development, and design validation.
Hands-on semiconductor wafer fabrication process and process integration challenges.
Reliability failure statistics, physics, failure mechanisms, and failure analysis methodologies.
Experience in of SPC/DOE principles, DOEs execution, and statistical analysis.
Data extraction and analysis skills (JMP/Crystal Ball/ILM/REL/PCS/SQL Scripting).
Knowledge of photonic datacom and telecom reliability qualification standards such as Telcordia GR-468, AEC-Q102.

Intel is shaping the future of data center computing through technologies powering critical cloud, AI, enterprise, and high-performance computing workloads.

This highly visible role operates at the intersection of technology, customers, and business strategy, translating market insights, customer needs, and technical trade-offs into product decisions that strengthen competitive positioning and deliver meaningful business outcomes.
The ideal candidate combines deep technical acumen, strategic thinking, customer focus, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across a highly matrixed organization.
What You'll Do

Product Ownership & Lifecycle Leadership
Own a Xeon product through its full lifecycle: product definition, planning, development, production, launch, and end‑of‑life.

Own workload and KPI readiness gates, driving execution across validation, debug, and performance optimization teams.
Represent product readiness, risks, and mitigation plans in executive and cross‑organizational reviews.
Support global product launches in partnership with marketing, communications, PR, and sales enablement teams.
Cross‑Functional Leadership
Align engineering, marketing, manufacturing, and business stakeholders on priorities, tradeoffs, and definitions of success.
Drive convergence across validation, debug, and performance teams to ensure outcomes reflect real customer requirements.
Operate effectively in a highly matrixed environment, influencing without direct authority.

Job Description:
Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.
Life at Intel
The Role and Impact
As a Strategic/Development Industrial Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and implementing solutions that drive Intel's manufacturing efficiency and long-term capacity planning capabilities. By analyzing complex business data, developing production models, and optimizing equipment and facility layouts, you will empower Intel to deliver world-class technologies while reducing costs and improving operational performance. Your work will directly contribute to Intel's ability to innovate and meet the demands of a dynamic global market.

Business group
You will join Intel Foundry's Factory Capacity Optimization (FCO) organization, a team responsible for factory space, capacity, and capital planning. This group leads Intel's growth strategy by enabling data-driven decisions that align with long-term manufacturing objectives. As part of the FCO Network Design team, you'll collaborate across manufacturing operations, technology development, and finance to support Intel's mission of delivering cutting-edge technologies with scalability and efficiency.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop and execute space, capacity, and capital strategies for APTM WPM (Advanced Packaging Technology Manufacturing - Wafer Packaging Manufacturing) factories to balancing near term execution and long range planning through scenario-based tradeoff analysis.
• Model WPM (Wafer Packaging Manufacturing) capacity across specific manufacturing segments, incorporating demand forecasts, tool roadmaps, and customer scenarios and demand-capacity tradeoffs to inform factory response options.
• Perform SnOP demand and capacity analysis evaluating gaps, constraints, and responses scenarios including one or more APTM manufacturing segments and translate insights into clear executive-ready recommendations on capacity actions, capital timing, and tradeoffs.
• Analyze tradeoffs between space, capacity, throughput, and CapEx to optimize factory economics and return on invested capital (ROIC), framing implications for decision timing and risk.
• Integrate capacity strategies across APTM organizations, Technology Development (TD), Manufacturing, Foundry Business Group (FBG), Foundry Construction and Sourcing, Foundry Customer Strategic Planning, and Finance to ensure alignment and executable decision timing.
• Collect, benchmark, and synthesize internal and external data to develop structured insights and recommendations for senior and executive leadership.
• Own and develop new planning or modeling capability within the organization, driving rapid maturity, adoption, and sustained impact.
• Communicate clearly under tight timelines and incomplete information, making sound assumptions when data is unavailable and upleveling insights to influence outcomes across a diverse cross-functional stakeholder set.

Job Description:
The Production Specialist supports the Systems Operations business unit by performing highly detailed relay assembly, adjustment, testing, and micro-cleaning processes in a clean room manufacturing environment. This role requires working with very small relay components under 10X–20X stereo magnification using precision tools and equipment to meet strict electrical and mechanical specifications. The position involves learning relay adjust-test station operations, magnetizing permanent magnets, fine-tuning relay performance, and following detailed work instructions for custom and QPL relay products. Success in this role requires strong manual dexterity, attention to detail, visual focus, and the ability to maintain quality and consistency in repetitive precision work

Fabricate certain relay assemblies, which may include contact assembly, first and second framing, vacuum baking, enclosure pressing, and preliminary electrical testing.
Perform the micro-clean process, as required and applicable, for space-grade relays.

Lead digital architecture, design, verification, and implementation of next-generation Power Management ICs (PMICs) for automotive and industrial applications.

Collaborate across analog, verification, validation, subsystem, SoC, applications, systems, product definition, and customer-facing teams to deliver high-quality mixed-signal solutions.
Job Responsibility:
Review product requirements, IP architecture specifications, programming models, microarchitecture, interfaces, and implementation plans for automotive and industrial PMIC applications.
Define and implement digital architectures for mixed-signal PMICs, ensuring alignment with system, performance, quality, reliability, safety, power, and area requirements.
Lead digital design activities from architecture definition through RTL development, integration, synthesis, timing closure, low-power implementation, silicon bring-up, and production release.
Design and develop digital control, monitoring, telemetry, diagnostics, configuration, protection, power sequencing, and fault management functions for PMIC and power conversion products.
Develop and review RTL, microarchitecture, and design specifications using Verilog/SystemVerilog and industry-standard design and quality checking tools.
Drive verification strategy and execution, including test planning, simulation, formal verification, coverage analysis, regression management, and achievement of NXP quality and maturity standards.
Deliver complete IP solutions, including RTL, verification collateral, supporting documentation, and requirements traceability from specification through implementation.
Track development metrics including milestones, code and functional coverage, defect resolution, and compliance with design requirements.
Support silicon debug, characterization, qualification, reliability validation, and production ramp activities.
Mentor junior engineers and drive continuous improvement in design methodologies, automation flows, and engineering best practices.

Experience with synthesis, static timing analysis, equivalence checking, DFT, and physical implementation flows.
Strong knowledge of modern verification methodologies, including UVM, assertions, formal verification, and coverage-driven verification.

Proficiency with industry-standard EDA tools from Cadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to develop innovative solutions for complex technical challenges.

About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Job Description
SoC Design Manager / Product Lead
Role Overview
ADI is seeking a highly experienced SoC Design Manager / Product Lead to lead the end-to-end execution of complex SoC and processor programs from concept to commercialization.
This role combines the responsibilities of a Chip Lead, Technical Program Leader, and Business Stakeholder Manager, owning overall product execution across architecture, silicon, software, validation, and business teams. The ideal candidate will drive cross-functional alignment, manage technical and program risk, engage with customers, and ensure successful product delivery.
Key Responsibilities
Own complete SoC development from architecture through tape-out, silicon bring-up, production ramp, and commercialization.
Provide technical leadership across architecture, RTL design, verification, DFT, physical design, software, and post-silicon activities.
Drive program execution, schedules, staffing plans, risk management, and milestone delivery.
Lead critical trade-off decisions involving performance, power, area, cost, quality, features, and schedule.
Partner with software, systems, product, and business teams to ensure strong hardware-software co-design.
Serve as the primary interface for customers, business units, and senior leadership on execution-related matters.
Support customer engagements and product vertical customer visits as needed.
Influence and align globally distributed teams across engineering, software, operations, product management, and business functions.
Drive production readiness, go-to-market planning, and successful product commercialization.
Qualifications
BS/MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
20+ years of semiconductor industry experience, including leadership of complex SoC/ASIC/Processor development programs.
Proven track record of multiple successful silicon tape-outs and product commercialization.
Strong expertise in SoC architecture, digital design, verification, DFT, physical design, silicon validation, and manufacturing.
Experience leading large cross-functional teams and influencing without direct authority.
Strong customer-facing, stakeholder management, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Success Criteria
Successful first-time tape-out and commercialization of complex SoCs.
Predictable program execution with effective risk management.
Strong hardware-software alignment throughout the development lifecycle.
Successful delivery of customer, product, and business objectives.
Executive confidence through clear communication and stakeholder leadership.
Alignment of diverse teams around a common product vision and execution strategy.
